judge_panel.reason: The paper explicitly addresses this in the Introduction: 'For the sake of simplicity, in the following both the axion solving the strong CP problem and a generic ALP will be referred to as axions, with explicit distinction made when referring to probes of the QCD axion.' The SN cooling bound in Sec. 2 states 'g_an=0' explicitly, and Sec. 3.2 states 'a minimal model is assumed in which axion production...as well as axion decays are uniquely determined by the axion-photon coupling.'

The manuscript does distinguish the cases: it states, "The main difference between the QCD axion and a generic ALP is in the relation between their mass and couplings" and adds that both will be called "axions," "with explicit distinction made when referring to probes of the QCD axion." It also spells out model assumptions in the flagged places, e.g. "for ma ≲ 30 MeV and gan = 0" and "a minimal model is assumed in which axion production ... as well as axion decays are uniquely determined by the axion-photon coupling."

The reviewer incorrectly claims that specific coupling assumptions and model choices are not stated with sufficient clarity. The paper explicitly writes, 'corresponding to axion-proton couplings... for ma ≲ 30 MeV and gan = 0' on page 3, and clearly defines the minimal model on page 6: 'For reference, a minimal model is assumed in which axion production... as well as axion decays are uniquely determined by the axion-photon coupling.'

Therefore, these regions would be appropriately constrained by observations from the Pierre Venus Orbiter (PVO), rather than SMM 33." The text does not specify which contour/region in Fig. 2 this refers to or whether the plotted exclusion already includes that replacement.

The text asserts that 'these regions would be appropriately constrained by observations from the Pierre Venus Orbiter (PVO), rather than SMM', but Figure 2 contains distinct exclusion contours for both 'PVO' and 'SN1987A (γ)'.
